name: Dice Roll Resolver
description: Dice, done honestly. Parses standard notation (2d6+3), rolls from a seeded stream, and appends every result to a bounded roll log, because a board game where a contested roll cannot be replayed is a board game whose luck arguments never end. The seed cursor advances deterministically per die and is emitted with each result, so any roll can be reproduced exactly — the same audit contract world.floor_descent applies to dungeons, applied to polyhedrals. This component owns uniform discrete dice only. Weighted tables with disclosed odds — gacha pools, drop rates — belong to utility.probability_core, whose published-rates input exists for odds that must be advertised; dice odds are disclosed by the notation itself. It does not own what a roll means: movement distance, space effects, and contests are decided by the components that asked for the roll.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: The stream every roll derives from. Required for the same reason world.floor_descent requires a run seed: unseeded dice cannot be audited, replayed, or argued about productively.

inputs.name: maxDicePerRoll
inputs.description: Guard against malformed notation asking for a million dice. Real systems rarely exceed ten.

inputs.name: explodeOnMax
inputs.description: Whether a max-face die rerolls and adds. A real mechanic in some systems; off by default because it changes every published probability the notation implies.

inputs.name: rollLogCapacity
inputs.description: How many rolls the audit log retains. Bounded so long sessions do not grow memory without bound; a thousand rolls is several game nights.

outputs.name: lastRoll
outputs.description: Notation, individual faces, modifier, total, and the seed cursor — the complete audit record of the most recent roll.

outputs.name: rollCount
outputs.description: Rolls since seed init. Also the index into the audit log.
